# `pi_station_remove`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Remove a saved station-mode Wi-Fi network profile from the device.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds, by command-socket invocation, which always writes shared diagnostics); the effect of the handler itself is probable |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xcda90 (64-bit build), ns_net::pi_station_remove @0x6fc9d0; supplied remove script |

Runs the device's network script synchronously to delete the profile whose SSID matches exactly. The script removes one matched profile per interface list, saves the default-interface configuration explicitly, and conditionally reconfigures the wireless interface when the removed profile was the active one. A success reply does not prove the profile was removed or that the connection dropped: neither the script exit status nor the individual remove/save results are checked.

Side effects: Deletes a saved network profile and persists the default-interface network configuration; may reconfigure the wireless interface and disconnect the current station link. Synchronous, no helper timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"pi_station_remove"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array\|string | yes | - | Station-network profile to remove. Three equivalent spellings: an object with ssid, an array whose first element is the SSID string, or the bare SSID string. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | ssid missing, null, empty array, or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 217 | ssid is the empty string | `string is empty` |
| 207 | Command output contains the text error (case-insensitive) | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

If the command runner itself fails, its thread-local error code is forwarded; the exact set of such codes is unresolved.

## Example

Request, object-form - Remove a profile by SSID:

```json
{"id":21,"method":"pi_station_remove","params":{"ssid":"ExampleNet"}}
```

Request, scalar-form - Bare string form:

```json
{"id":22,"method":"pi_station_remove","params":"ExampleNet"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_remove","result":0,"code":0,"id":21}
```

Reply, empty-ssid:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_remove","error":"string is empty","code":217,"id":23}
```
